decisions.question: Renumber the page keys to follow the grouped page bar?
decisions.context: The page bar is now grouped into Play (Home, Mods, Tests, Logs, Memory, Game files, Atlas), Code (Changes, Timeline, Code map, Make-up) and Tools (Reports, Settings, Decisions). The keys still follow the old order: 1 Home, 2 Reports, 3 Atlas, 4 Tests, 5 Mods, 6 Changes, 7 Timeline, 8 Code map, 9 Settings, G Logs, M Make-up, D Decisions. Memory (U) and Game files (W) keep their letters either way.

options.label: Renumber them
options.detail: 1 Home, 2 Mods, 3 Tests, 4 Logs, 5 Atlas, 6 Changes, 7 Timeline, 8 Code map, 9 Make-up; E Reports, S Settings, D Decisions. G and M are freed. Keys you changed yourself stay as you set them

options.label: Keep them as they are
options.detail: No key changes; the numbers no longer match the bar's order

decisions.why: The number keys would count along the bar you see; they are a day old, so little is lost in learning them again

decisions.question: Should agents in every repository put the choices they make for you on this page?
decisions.context: Today only the Companion's own agent choices are here. As a shared rule, every repository (phobos-rimworld and the rest) would list its agent choices and open questions in its own config/decisions.json, and this page would gather them all.

options.label: Yes, every repository
options.detail: A shared rule in phobos-modkit's rules; design records still label choices as now

options.label: Only the Companion's
options.detail: Other repositories keep their choices in their design records

decisions.why: Choices scattered across design records are easy to miss; one page with buttons is the point of this page

decisions.question: Build the last two cross-links: design records joined to code (S1) and rules joined to the checks that enforce them (S5)?
decisions.context: Both are in docs/cross-links.md and docs/later.md. S1 would show, beside a design record's section, the code that builds it; S5, beside each rule, the check that holds it.

options.label: After the game-files work
options.detail: Saves, screenshots and what changed since you last played come first

decisions.why: The game-files views are more use day to day; S1 and S5 serve agents more than you

decisions.question: Add 'Size as installed' to Make-up?
decisions.context: Make-up measures lines, size in the repository and files. Size as installed would measure what each mod takes in the game's Mods folder, encoded textures included.
decisions.why: Textures make installed size very different from repository size, and the install records already know where each mod is

decisions.question: Mark a moment in a memory watch without leaving the game?
decisions.context: Today a mark needs the Companion in front: Alt+Tab, B, a few words, Enter, then back to the game. The page's own keys are one key each, but a key that works while the game is in front has to be two held together, or the game would lose that key. It needs a new library (Tauri's global shortcut plugin).

options.label: Add a key that works in the game
options.detail: Ctrl+Alt+M (changeable) marks the moment at once as 'marked from the game', without leaving the game; add words on the Memory page afterwards

options.label: Keep marks in the Companion's window
options.detail: Alt+Tab, B, words, Enter, as now

decisions.why: Switching windows mid-reload is the moment marks matter most and the moment you are least free to type; one press keeps the time exact and spares the mouse

decisions.question: Teach the Code map to read TypeScript, Svelte and Rust, so the tools entry's own code can be followed?
decisions.context: 0.24.0 lists your tools (the Companion, the kit and the logger) beside your games. The Code map reads C#, XML Defs, Lua and Python, so it follows the kit's Python but not the Companion's Svelte, TypeScript or Rust: for phobos-companion it says nothing was read. Ostranauts and RimWorld are C#; none of your games' mods use these three.

options.label: All three
options.detail: New readers in the kit for TypeScript, Svelte and Rust: calls, imports, components and Tauri commands joined window to host

options.label: TypeScript and Svelte first
options.detail: The window's code; Rust after

options.label: Later
options.detail: Leave the Code map to your games' languages for now

decisions.why: The join that matters most is a window request to the host command that answers it, and that needs both sides read

decisions.question: Should Check what they mean for ours run by itself after an update, or only when you press it?
decisions.context: On the Mods page, Since you last played now offers Check what they mean for ours (0.35.0). It may decompile new builds into the tools' cache, and its first run after an update took about two minutes on your game; later runs take seconds.

options.label: Only when I press it
options.detail: As What did an update change? and Keep the new builds: nothing runs the decompiler without your press

options.label: By itself, once after each update
options.detail: When Since you last played sees an update, the check starts by itself and its bar shows on the Mods page

decisions.why: It matches your choice of 19 Nov 2026 (Read and compare, on your press), and keeps the Mods page quick to open after a big round of updates
decisions.from: docs/design-record.md, Check what they mean for ours

decisions.question: Which key should open the Explorer (saves and the running game)?
decisions.context: The Explorer (docs/debugging.md, docs/save-explorer.md; your choice of 20 Nov 2026: one page for saves and the running game) sits under Play, after Game files, and opens on V for now (0.41.0). O, Q, S, Y and Z are free too; E and S are proposed for Reports and Settings if the page keys are renumbered.

options.label: V
options.detail: Free today and not wanted by the renumbering proposal

options.label: O, for open
options.detail: Also free today

decisions.why: It stays free whichever way the page keys go, and every key can be changed in Settings anyway

decisions.question: Should Go to anything search inside a save as you type, or offer one Search this save entry?
decisions.context: Go to anything (/) searches pages, code, changelog entries, test rows, settings and reports. A save holds hundreds of thousands of things; searching it is quick once the save has been read, but reading it the first time takes a moment.

options.label: One Search this save entry
options.detail: Pressing it opens the save explorer with the search filled in; Go to anything itself stays as quick as now

options.label: Search the save as I type
options.detail: Things from the newest save appear among the other results; slower, and only once that save has been read

decisions.why: Go to anything stays instant, and a save's results are many enough to need the explorer's own list

decisions.question: Which key should open the Search page once it is built?
decisions.context: Search (docs/search.md) is reached from Go to anything's top row, Everything about "…". It can also have its own page key. S and Y are free everywhere today; S is also proposed for Settings if the page keys are renumbered.

options.label: S, for search
options.detail: Easy to remember; Settings would then keep 9 if the keys are renumbered

options.label: Y
options.detail: Free and wanted by nothing else

options.label: No key of its own
options.detail: Reached from Go to anything (/) only

decisions.why: Search is something you will reach for often, and S says what it does

decisions.question: Where should a new search start: in the part of the program you came from, or everywhere?
decisions.context: You asked for contexts so a search does not show literally everything at once (docs/search.md). Widening to everywhere is always one press, and the overview says how many more matches lie outside.

options.label: The part I came from
options.detail: From the Mods or Logs page it starts in Play; from Changes, in Code

options.label: Everywhere
options.detail: Every source at once, overview first; narrow it with a chip

options.label: The context I used last
options.detail: Remembered between searches

decisions.why: It keeps the first answer small, as you asked, without a choice to make first

decisions.question: Where should the Safe copies card live?
decisions.context: Safe copies (0.42.0) show each training set and style model, whether it is copied, changed since its copy or never copied, with Copy now and Check the copies. The hand-off's question 4 was not asked, so it went to Home, below the records note.

options.label: A card on Home
options.detail: Where you already look first; it is outlined when something has never been copied or has changed since

options.label: A card on the Mods page
options.detail: Beside the install backups; Home would show nothing about it

options.label: A page of its own
options.detail: Room for a history of runs and a restore button later; Home would keep a one-line note when something waits

decisions.why: A warning that a training was never copied belongs where you look first, and the card is small
